key_insight: A-site high-entropy disorder and tensile strain jointly tune nickelate defects and electronic states, improving oxygen evolution activity while the high-entropy material resists degradation better than LaNiO3.
engineering_relevance: Combining rare-earth mixing with epitaxial strain offers a route to more active and durable perovskite oxide electrocatalysts.
method: Studied epitaxial (La0.2Pr0.2Nd0.2Sm0.2Eu0.2)NiO3 films under different strain conditions.
Probed structural defects, Ni valence, electronic states, and OER performance.
Used first-principles calculations to investigate strain-dependent rare-earth orbital hybridization.
evidence_signal: Tensile-strained films showed earlier OER onset, stronger pre-catalytic Ni redox features, and higher activity than compressively strained films and representative single-A-site nickelates; the high-entropy material also resisted structural degradation better than LaNiO3.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative activity or durability benchmarks, and transfer from epitaxial films to scalable electrodes remains unestablished.
paper_title: High-Entropy A-Site Disorder Enhances Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity and Stability in Nickelate Thin Films
